raw_response:
I’ve been farming these fields for 60 years, since I was a little boy following my father around with a hoe. Never spent a day in school, but I know this land—every slope, every wet patch, every spot where the weeds come up thick. My wife and me, we’re the only ones left in the house now. The children went to Shijiazhuang and Beijing years ago. So it’s just us two old bones working 11.6 mu. We plant a bit of everything because if one crop fails or the price drops, we still have something to eat and a little cash for medicine.

This year I’ll put 3 mu in cotton, 3 mu in spring maize, 3.6 mu in peanut, and 2 mu in mungbean. I don’t have much cash saved up—maybe three thousand yuan I can spend on inputs. Every yuan has to be watched.

The cotton goes in around April 20th when the soil warms up. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, two bags for the 3 mu. For fertilizer, I put down one big bag of that compound fertilizer for every mu at planting—that’s what I’ve always done. When the cotton starts flowering in July, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. I’ll irrigate twice from my well, but pumping costs electricity money, so I only water when the leaves start curling in the afternoon. Cotton worms are bad around here, so I spray four or five times with whatever insecticide Old Wang at the supply store says is working this year. Picking is hard on our backs. If my wife’s sciatica acts up, I might hire two women from the village for a few days, but they want 80 yuan a day now, so I’d rather pick it ourselves, even if it takes longer.

The spring maize goes in right after the cotton, late April. I saved most of the seed from last year, so I only need to buy a little to refresh it. One bag of compound fertilizer for the 3 mu at planting, then I spread some urea when the plants are knee-high. If the summer rains come like they did two years ago, one irrigation is enough. I spray herbicide once and insecticide maybe twice.

Peanuts I plant in early May on the sandier plot on the east side. Peanuts need that calcium fertilizer, so I buy a bag of that along with the compound fertilizer. Two irrigations should do, maybe three if the drought continues like last year. I spray for disease because two years ago some of the pods rotted in the ground and I lost money.

Mungbeans are the easiest. I plant them in early June on the 2 mu near the well. Just a handful of compound fertilizer at planting, weed them twice by hand, and harvest in August. Good food for us, and I can sell a few jin to the collection man who drives through the village.

All told, I reckon I’ll spend about 3,100 yuan on seeds, fertilizer, medicine, water, and hiring a bit of help. It’s a lot for two old people, but you have to spend money to make money. I just hope the rain comes at the right time and the prices don’t collapse.
